summary.headline: The Community Preservation Committee reviewed restructured bids for the Town Common rail project, prepared for Town Meeting, and advanced CPA project signage.
summary.summary: The Community Preservation Committee reviewed a value-engineered bid structure for the Town Common rail restoration after initial cost estimates came in nearly double the expected budget. Members established floor assignments and procedural plans for the upcoming Annual Town Meeting on April 11. The committee also set a summer timeline to review four continued project applications ahead of Fall Town Meeting and reviewed a comprehensive inventory and design plan for permanent CPA project signage across town.

topics.title: Town Common rail restoration project update
topics.summary: Project representatives reported that initial cost estimates from consultant VHB came in nearly double the expected budget. The town restructured the bid documents into a base project with two add-alternates to keep work within the authorized budget.
key_details: Base project covers scraping, painting, and restoring existing railing.
Add-alternate 1 covers adding fixtures and bolts.
Add-alternate 2 covers replacing granite posts and installing new railing sections where needed.
Bid documents will be issued on April 1 with bids due April 22, 2026.
The contract documents require construction to be completed within the current calendar year.
topics.outcome: Bids will be opened in late April, and representatives will update the committee in May before contract award.
topics.why_it_matters: Determines whether the long-planned Town Common rail restoration can proceed without requiring additional funding from town meeting.

topics.title: Golf course Audubon International certification update
topics.summary: Open Space Preservation Commission Chair Freddie Gillespie provided an update on a $15,000 project originally approved at the 2018 Town Meeting to establish an ecological management plan for the Southborough Golf Course. The commission is working with the conservation agent to issue a request for proposals to hire a consultant to write the plan, aiming for Audubon International certification.
key_details: Town Meeting appropriated $15,000 in 2018, with approximately $500 expended to date.
The project supports ecological management, chemical and water monitoring, and wildlife habitat preservation on the municipal golf course.
Audubon International previously waived back annual membership fees and reinstated the town program.
An RFP is being drafted with the conservation agent for review by the Open Space Preservation Commission and Golf Course Committee.
topics.outcome: The committee expects an RFP to be finalized so work can begin in the spring, with a further progress report scheduled for May.

topics.title: Annual Town Meeting preparation and assignments
topics.summary: With Town Meeting set for April 11, the committee coordinated member roles and floor presentations in the chair's anticipated absence. Members also reviewed whether the Affordable Housing Trust would present slides or provide informational handouts.
key_details: The committee chair will be absent from the April 11 Town Meeting due to travel.
Vice Chair Kristin LaVault will move the annual CPC budget and discretionary transfer articles on the town meeting floor.
Member Grant Farrington agreed to move the Affordable Housing Trust article.
Affordable Housing Trust representative Ellen Marya confirmed the trust will distribute a printed informational handout rather than deliver a slide presentation.
A committee meeting was scheduled for 9:30 AM in the auditorium prior to the 10:00 AM Town Meeting start in case an emergency quorum is required.
topics.outcome: Floor motions and responsibilities were assigned for the April 11, 2026 Annual Town Meeting.

topics.title: Review process for Fall Town Meeting applications
topics.summary: The committee established deadlines and expectations for four project applications that were continued from the spring cycle to the Fall Town Meeting. Members agreed on target dates to ensure full review before warrant articles close.
key_details: Four applications are being prepared for Fall Town Meeting: Fayville Park improvements, Rural Cemetery water tower restoration, Golf Course irrigation, and Peninsula Trail boardwalk/bridge work.
Recreation has scheduled public input forums on Fayville Park for April 14 and May 20, 2026.
The Historical Commission is evaluating whether to proceed with the cemetery water tower engineering study or incorporate it into a broader cemetery expansion and columbarium concept.
The committee set an internal goal of having final warrant articles drafted by August 31, 2026, aiming to conclude substantial review by the end of July.
topics.outcome: Applicants will be asked to submit updated scopes, revised applications, and firm cost estimates ahead of the May and June meetings.

topics.title: CPA project signage program and inventory
topics.summary: Member Ellen Marya presented an inventory spreadsheet and draft visual mockups for permanent bronze and PVC signs to mark past and ongoing projects funded by the Community Preservation Act. Committee members discussed assigning specific projects to individual members to coordinate wording, mounting styles, and sign placement with relevant town boards and departments.
key_details: Inventory covers more than 20 past CPA projects across town.
Bronze plaques are proposed for historic preservation projects, while PVC signs are proposed for recreation and open space sites.
Sign funding will come directly from remaining balances in individual project accounts prior to project closeout.

Members volunteered to liaise with specific departments: fire and police chiefs for the public safety memorial, Recreation for park and court sites, Historical Commission for historic schools and burial grounds, and library trustees for the library facade.
topics.outcome: Members will reach out to assigned boards and departments to confirm proposed wording and mounting locations before placing sign orders.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee reviewed and approved meeting minutes from three previous sessions and set their next regular meeting date.
key_details: Meeting minutes of November 19, 2025 were approved as amended.
Meeting minutes of December 3, 2025 were approved as amended.
Meeting minutes of February 19, 2026 were approved as amended.
The next regular meeting was scheduled for May 20, 2026, at 7:00 PM.
topics.outcome: Minutes approved and next meeting scheduled.

public_comment.summary: A resident emphasized the importance of setting clear project plans with measurable milestones for town projects, noting that an eight-year span without completion on the Audubon project is excessive.

A resident suggested standardizing CPA signage with a simple, tasteful sign bearing a QR code and URL linking to a town webpage, arguing it would save costs, avoid sign clutter, and allow the town to easily update project details and history.
